diagnoses.location: Workflow 2 > Semantic Contract Gate for Keyed Event Aggregations > contributing-event predicate list
diagnoses.defect: The 'Semantic Contract Gate' enumerates only one predicate (contributing-event) and omits the other two predicates that the section header promises ('three separate predicates'). In particular, it does not define a 'completion/terminal event' predicate (which event types mark a key as finished) nor an 'emission eligibility' predicate (when a key is allowed to produce output). This directly matches the location hint about missing rules for '完成事件判定' (completion event determination) in Workflow 2.
diagnoses.evidence: Section text: 'write down and preserve three separate predicates: 1. Contributing-event predicate: ...' — list ends after item 1, with no items 2 or 3 defined.

diagnoses.location: Workflow 2 > Semantic Contract Gate > validation bullets
diagnoses.defect: The validation guidance mentions that 'a key with qualifying activity and the required completion event must be emitted', but the skill never previously defines what 'required completion event' means nor states the inverse rule (keys without a qualifying completion/terminal event must NOT be emitted). This matches the second location hint about missing rules for '结果输出资格' (output eligibility). Without an explicit negative/eligibility rule, implementers can emit results for every key seen in the activity stream, producing extra keys even when expected keys are all present (which the current bullet acknowledges but does not instruct how to prevent).
diagnoses.evidence: Bullet: 'compare the output key set as well as aggregate values, and investigate unexpected extra keys even when all expected keys are present.' — but no rule tells the implementer that extra keys indicate a missing eligibility gate on the completion predicate.

repair_plan.target: senior-data-engineer/SKILL.md — Workflow 2 > Semantic Contract Gate for Keyed Event Aggregations
repair_plan.change: Complete the enumerated list of three predicates by adding (2) a 'Completion/terminal-event predicate' and (3) an 'Emission-eligibility predicate'. The completion predicate must instruct the implementer to explicitly enumerate the full set of event types that mark a key as finished (including non-success terminations such as failure/kill/abort), to source terminality from the authoritative lifecycle stream rather than inferring it from activity events, and to document which event types are explicitly NON-terminal (e.g., scheduling/update events) so they are not mistakenly treated as completion.

repair_plan.target: senior-data-engineer/SKILL.md — Workflow 2 > Semantic Contract Gate (same section)
repair_plan.change: Add the third predicate: 'Emission-eligibility predicate' stating that a per-key result MUST be emitted only when the key has at least one contributing event AND has observed a terminal event per the completion predicate. Explicitly state the negative rule: keys observed only via contributing (activity) events without a terminal event must be suppressed. Clarify that emission happens once per eligible key at end-of-stream (bounded sources) or on terminal trigger.

repair_plan.target: senior-data-engineer/SKILL.md — Workflow 2 > Semantic Contract Gate > validation bullets
repair_plan.change: Extend validation to include both a positive and a negative fixture: (a) a key with activity + terminal event must appear in output; (b) a key with activity but no terminal event must NOT appear in output. Instruct that any extra keys in the output set are a signal of a missing or mis-specified completion/eligibility predicate and must be traced back to those two predicates.
